# forward

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/app/forward"
```

Package forward is the public facade for store and forward: an export that waits on disk while the collector it is meant for is down, and a count of what it held, sent and lost (ADR 0185).

A [Forwarder](#Forwarder) holds each batch as one message of a durable queue (package [github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/queue](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/data/queue): a directory, a table, or memory) and sends it later through a [Sender](#Sender) its caller supplies. [Forwarder](#Forwarder).Enqueue returns once the batch is durable; [Forwarder](#Forwarder).Run sends, one batch at a time by default, each retried on the forwarder's clock while [Config](#Config).Retryable calls its failure retryable and the batch is younger than [Config](#Config).MaxAge — waiting the delay a collector imposes (a Retry-After) in full, otherwise a backoff from five to thirty seconds. A batch the sender refuses for good is dead-lettered in the queue; one that outlives its age is dropped. The queue is bounded in batches and in bytes, and [Config](#Config).WhenFull says what happens at the bound: [DropOldest](#DropOldest) (the zero), [DropNewest](#DropNewest), or [Block](#Block) for a bounded time. [Forwarder](#Forwarder).Stats counts what is pending, sent, retried, dropped, expired and dead-lettered, and the last delay a collector imposed.

For telemetry, the producer is an adapter put where the network exporter was, and the sender is the network exporter's DocumentExporter:

```
otlp, err := trace.NewOTLPHTTPExporter("otlp", trace.OTLPHTTPConfig{Endpoint: endpoint})
document, _ := otlp.(trace.DocumentExporter)
broker, err := queue.NewFile(queue.FileConfig{Dir: "/var/lib/app/spans", Policy: policy})
fw, err := forward.New(ctx, forward.Config{
	Broker:    broker,
	Send:      document.ExportDocument,
	Retryable: trace.OTLPRetryable,
})
go fw.Run(ctx) // or under lifecycle.NewSupervisor
spans, err := forward.NewSpanExporter("otlp-durable", fw) // behind a trace.BatchSink
```

One queue per signal: metrics take their own forwarder, through [NewMetricExporter](#NewMetricExporter) and the metrics exporter's DocumentExporter. A batch is sent at least once: a process that dies between the collector's acceptance and the acknowledgement sends it again, which OTLP tolerates.

<a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/app/forward/gen_facade.go>)

Config is the public alias for a forwarder's configuration: Broker, Send and Retryable required; Clock, MaxBatches, MaxBytes, WhenFull, BlockTimeout, SendTimeout, MaxAge, Backoff, Parallelism, PollInterval, DrainTimeout and SettleTimeout optional.

```go
type Config = svcforward.Config
```

Config is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/forward.Config`, declared as:

```go
type Config struct {
	// Broker is the queue the forwarder holds its batches in: a directory
	// (queue.NewFile) for a backlog that outlives the process, a table
	// (queue.NewSQL), or memory. One queue per signal. Build it with a
	// VisibilityTimeout above SendTimeout, a MaxDeliveries no outage reaches
	// — MaxAge is the forwarder's budget — and a MaxMessageBytes that holds
	// a batch. The forwarder neither sets its policy nor closes it.
	Broker        corequeue.Broker
	// Send ships one stored batch: an OTLP/HTTP exporter's ExportDocument,
	// or any function of that shape.
	Send          Sender
	// Retryable classifies a failure of Send as one a later attempt may cure
	// — trace.OTLPRetryable, metrics.OTLPRetryable. It is REQUIRED: nil reads
	// as "retry everything" or as "retry nothing", two opposites. A failure
	// it calls permanent is dead-lettered at once.
	Retryable     func(error) bool
	// Clock paces every retry, bounds every attempt and the wait of Block,
	// and ages every batch. Nil means clock.System; a clock.ManualClock drives
	// a test without a sleep. It must be the broker's: a batch's age is read
	// from the instant the broker stamped.
	Clock         clock.Timed
	// MaxBatches bounds the batches the forwarder holds. Zero means
	// DefaultMaxBatches; negative is refused.
	MaxBatches    int
	// MaxBytes bounds the bytes the forwarder holds. Zero means
	// DefaultMaxBytes; negative is refused. A batch larger on its own is
	// refused with BatchTooLarge.
	MaxBytes      int64
	// WhenFull is what Enqueue does when either bound is reached. The zero
	// is DropOldest.
	WhenFull      FullPolicy
	// BlockTimeout bounds the wait of Block. Zero means DefaultBlockTimeout;
	// negative is refused.
	BlockTimeout  time.Duration
	// SendTimeout bounds one attempt, on Clock. Zero means
	// DefaultSendTimeout; negative is refused.
	SendTimeout   time.Duration
	// MaxAge is how long after the queue accepted it a batch may still be
	// sent: one delivered older is dropped unsent, one whose retryable
	// failure finds it older is not retried; either is acknowledged and
	// counted Expired. A Retry-After is honoured in full, but never past it.
	// Zero means DefaultMaxAge; negative is refused.
	MaxAge        time.Duration
	// Backoff is the wait before each retry when the failure imposes none:
	// Backoff.Delay(attempt). The zero value is the
	// DefaultRetryBase–DefaultRetryMax curve, and a curve without a positive
	// BaseDelay starts from DefaultRetryBase under its own ceiling: a failed
	// batch is never retried at once.
	Backoff       kbackoff.Value
	// Parallelism is how many consumers send at once. Non-positive is one,
	// which keeps the queue's order while nothing fails and sends one request
	// at a time to a collector that is down; above one there is no order.
	Parallelism   int
	// PollInterval is how late a batch another PROCESS queued may be
	// noticed; one Enqueue queued in this process is sent at once. Zero is
	// the queue's own default.
	PollInterval  time.Duration
	// DrainTimeout is how long the batch being sent when Run's context ends
	// may still run. Zero stops it at once; it is then handed back uncounted
	// and sent by the next process.
	DrainTimeout  time.Duration
	// SettleTimeout bounds each acknowledgement and hand-back once Run's
	// context has ended. Zero is the queue's own default.
	SettleTimeout time.Duration
}
```

<a name="Forwarder.Enqueue"></a>
### func \(Forwarder\) [Enqueue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/forward/forwarder.go>)

```go
func (*Forwarder) Enqueue(ctx context.Context, batch []byte) error
```

Enqueue keeps batch in the queue, durably once it returns nil, for Run to send. An empty batch is kept nowhere. A batch larger than MaxBytes is refused with BatchTooLarge; one the queue has no room for is handled by Config.WhenFull — older batches dropped, or ForwardFull, or a bounded wait — and every batch lost to a bound is counted Dropped. ctx bounds the publication and the wait.

<a name="Forwarder.Run"></a>
### func \(Forwarder\) [Run](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/app/forward/forwarder.go>)

```go
func (*Forwarder) Run(ctx context.Context) error
```

Run sends the queued batches until ctx ends, one consumer per Config.Parallelism, and returns what the queue's consumer returns. The batch being sent when ctx ends may finish within Config.DrainTimeout; one cut short is handed back uncounted and sent by the next process.

Stats is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/app/forward.StatsValue`, declared as:

```go
type Stats struct {
	// LastRetryAfterAt is when a collector last imposed a delay; zero when
	// none has.
	LastRetryAfterAt time.Time
	// PendingBytes is the bytes of the batches the forwarder holds.
	PendingBytes     int64
	// LastRetryAfter is the last delay a collector imposed — a Retry-After
	// — as the failure carried it.
	LastRetryAfter   time.Duration
	// Pending is the batches the forwarder holds: queued, waiting or being
	// sent.
	Pending          int
	// Enqueued counts the batches Enqueue kept.
	Enqueued         uint64
	// Sent counts the batches the sender accepted.
	Sent             uint64
	// Retries counts the attempts made after a retryable failure.
	Retries          uint64
	// Dropped counts the batches lost to a bound: refused by a full queue or
	// as too large, or taken out of it by DropOldest.
	Dropped          uint64
	// Expired counts the batches dropped because they outlived MaxAge.
	Expired          uint64
	// DeadLettered counts the batches the sender refused for good, kept in
	// the broker's dead-letter store.
	DeadLettered     uint64
}
```
